claims.text: The elevated-temperature stress–strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is influenced by its microstructure and composition.
The elevated-temperature thermal expansion of HfNbTaTiZr is influenced by its microstructure and composition.
The elevated-temperature elastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is influenced by its microstructure and composition.
The properties of HfNbTaTiZr can be optimized using in situ neutron diffraction and transmission electron microscopy.
Elevated-temperature deformation of HfNbTaTiZr may involve dislocation glide.
Elevated-temperature deformation of HfNbTaTiZr may involve twinning.
Elevated-temperature deformation of HfNbTaTiZr may involve grain-boundary sliding.
Microstructure and composition influence the operative deformation mechanisms in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed hypothesis may hold from above room temperature up to the melting point or beyond.
A lack of significant correlation between microstructure or composition and all three measured responses would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The proposed range extends beyond the melting point, whereas dislocation glide, twinning, and grain-boundary sliding are solid-state mechanisms and do not coherently describe a fully molten alloy.

Characterization techniques are presented as interventions that optimize or influence properties, although neutron diffraction and microscopy ordinarily measure the material rather than constitute a microstructure-modifying treatment.
